verdict.rationale: Honeybadger documents user-configured rules that run unattended in the background. Alarms evaluate a BadgerQL query against a threshold and fire alerts. Anomaly detection watches error volume against a learned baseline. Open errors are auto-resolved when a deploy is recorded, and uptime checks and check-ins monitor continuously. These are fixed monitoring and alerting automations, not general or agentic workflows; the MCP server only lets an external assistant query data on demand. Missing for 10: user-defined multi-step automation or workflow rules, autonomous agent actions (e.g., auto-triage or remediation), scheduling of arbitrary tasks, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
